stories.Headline: Nitrogen Brings Its AI-Powered Advisor Platform to Claude and ChatGPT, Expands Nucleus Capabilities
stories.Summary:
The supplied articles do not contain anything about Nitrogen, its advisor platform, or its Nucleus capabilities, so a story on that subject cannot be written from them. What they do cover is related material about AI assistants and money, and the facts below come only from that coverage. Anthropic introduced a dedicated Personal Finance feature inside Claude on November 5, 2026. It lets eligible subscribers connect supported bank accounts, credit cards, loans and investment accounts through Plaid, a financial technology service that links applications with participating institutions. The feature began rolling out in beta to Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers in the United States, and it is available on Claude's web, desktop and mobile applications.

Access is being introduced gradually rather than all at once. Once accounts are connected, Claude can review transactions, identify common spending categories, and flag subscriptions, regular payments and upcoming bills. It also organizes incoming and outgoing money into a cash flow overview and presents balances and spending activity through visual dashboards. Users can ask about budgets, savings targets and planned purchases, and the tool can point out unusual charges, duplicate transactions and rising bills.

Anthropic states that Claude can access selected account details, balances, credit limits and up to 24 months of transactions. OpenAI introduced its competing Finances feature in ChatGPT on May 15, 2026, and it also relies on Plaid to connect supported accounts. ChatGPT can organize expenses, help with monthly budgets, support savings calculations for future purchases and arrange available investment details for easier review. OpenAI has since added weekly financial insights, credit monitoring, stock watchlists, voice support and manual account entry.

A comparison published by Engadget examines where the two services overlap and where they differ. On privacy, Anthropic says conversations inside Claude's dedicated Personal Finance hub are not used to train its models, though conversations outside that hub remain subject to the user's regular privacy settings. ChatGPT follows the account's existing data controls, and users can turn off model training through the Improve the model for everyone setting under Data Controls. Both services use read-only access for their connected account features, so they cannot pay bills, transfer funds or execute investment transactions.

The coverage notes that responses can contain errors and that balances may not reflect the latest transactions, so users should check figures against official statements. Separately, Mashable promoted the Lifetime AI Software Stack Bundle at $47.99, down from a regular price of $1,811.99, with code DEAL20 through November 15. The bundle includes five tools, among them AskAnyModel AI, which shows answers from up to six models side by side. A Japanese press release dated November 9 also described HIX AI releasing a feature that compares answers from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other models on one screen.

stories.Headline: The Nvidia spy scandal exposes networks operating in Singapore that help Chinese tech companies access advanced US AI chips and circumvent export controls (Owen Walker/Financial Times)
stories.Summary:
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang acknowledged in an email to employees on Sunday, Nov. 8, that he had an extramarital relationship, writing that he was unfaithful to his wife and apologizing to his family. The relationship was with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at the Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The New York Times reported that US investigators suspected she had been recruited by Chinese intelligence, though the Korea Herald stresses that this suspicion has not been established as fact. Nvidia has previously described the contacts as routine business dealings. The Financial Times headline on the affair says it exposes Singapore's role in China's AI chip trade, but the article's text was behind a paywall and gave no further detail.

Nvidia's independent directors, assisted by outside counsel, will examine whether Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation, and he pledged to cooperate with that internal investigation. The board said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised, and it expressed confidence in him, so he remains in his position. Three US House committee chairs have requested a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18 about his contacts with Alice Huang and Nvidia's safeguards against espionage. Businesskorea reported that key Republican and Democratic lawmakers received a closed-door security briefing on Nov. 9 from CIA Director John Ratcliffe and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. That briefing was expected to cover how far the repercussions could reach US national security, based on what authorities had identified so far.

The Korea Herald reported that no new US restrictions had been announced in connection with the case. Businesskorea forecast that political pressure from Congress on Nvidia's Chinese operations would rise and that technology curbs on China could be tightened. Democratic senators are urging passage of the AI OVERWATCH act, which would restrict exports of advanced AI chips to China, and the MATCH Act, which would regulate exports of chipmaking equipment. They are also pushing the Chip Security Act, which would require tracking the location and usage of chips exported overseas. Businesskorea said Jensen Huang had argued for easing export rules on advanced chips on the logic that excessive limits could help Chinese companies grow, and that President Donald Trump partly accepted this and allowed exports of some older Nvidia chips to China.

Samsung Electronics and SK hynix could face tighter export compliance requirements if Washington steps up scrutiny, according to the Korea Herald. Stricter checks could mean extra verification of end users, intended applications and reexports, which would raise compliance costs and could delay shipments across the AI chip supply chain. Curbs that reduce Nvidia's sales to China could also indirectly hurt demand for the high-bandwidth memory used in its accelerators, though the real effect would depend on the scope of any measures and on demand elsewhere. Businesskorea added that the joint development of next-generation HBM with Nvidia could be affected, and that modernization and equipment replacement at the two companies' factories in China could face restrictions. An industry official told Businesskorea there may be little short-term impact but the long term is hard to predict.

The Korea Herald also noted possible upsides for Korean firms, since Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta are developing their own AI processors alongside Nvidia GPUs. Wider use of those chips could broaden the customer base for HBM and customized memory, and could help Korean AI chip developers such as Rebellions, although any gains would depend on commercial demand. Vice Science Minister Ryu Je-myung told a parliamentary budget committee on Monday that Seoul expects Nvidia GPU deliveries under existing contracts to proceed without disruption. He said 10,000 GPUs bought through last year's supplementary budget were already in use and that deliveries under this year's orders were underway. Separately, Madison Huang, the CEO's daughter and a senior Nvidia executive, canceled a planned Seoul visit, and Nvidia Vice President Deepu Talla replaced her at a startup partnership forum during Nvidia AI Day Seoul.

stories.Headline: What Does CoreWeave (CRWV) Winning A New AI Training Deal Mean?
stories.Summary:
CoreWeave has agreed a multi-year AI cloud infrastructure deal with Wayve, a British autonomous driving company, according to reports dated November 9, 2026. Under the agreement, Wayve will use CoreWeave's NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs to train and test its autonomous vehicle AI models. The capacity is described as dedicated AI cloud infrastructure tailored to large-scale physical AI workloads for driving development. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

CoreWeave stock rose 6% to $49.18 in afternoon trading on the day the deal was reported. One article puts the company's market value at $25.6 billion and describes it as a US-based cloud infrastructure provider supplying high-performance computing capacity for workloads such as AI training. Wayve already uses Weights & Biases, which CoreWeave acquired in 2025. The deal comes as CoreWeave has been expanding globally, including new data centers and a growing AI network built for compute-intensive use cases.

The articles are commentary and market reports rather than statements from the companies, so no executives are quoted on the Wayve agreement itself. Simply Wall St, in an article produced with the assistance of AI automation, said the deal backs the view that demand for AI infrastructure remains strong and that CoreWeave's specialized cloud is attracting large, technically demanding clients. It added that the agreement reinforces the idea that proprietary tooling and differentiated infrastructure are being adopted for real-world programs rather than just proof-of-concept pilots. That article also noted it had flagged one warning sign for CoreWeave, though it did not describe it, and pointed to a fair value of $135 in its analysis.

The Wayve news arrived on a day when AI cloud stocks rose while NVIDIA, the supplier of much of their hardware, fell 5% to $177.40 amid reports that the company is investigating CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Cloudflare jumped 11% to $297.22 after a third-quarter report in which revenue rose 39.2% year over year to $782.51 million. Nebius gained 9% to $140.70 ahead of its own earnings report, which is expected before the market opens on November 12. Oracle rose 3% to $119.16, and IREN rose 2% to $21.98.

CoreWeave and Nebius both rent GPU computing capacity to AI labs, hyperscalers and enterprises, and both buy their chips from NVIDIA. CoreWeave reported a revenue backlog of approximately $104 billion as of June 30, while Nebius disclosed $37.5 billion in remaining performance obligations. The next checkpoint for CoreWeave is its third-quarter 2026 earnings release and call, listed for November 10, 2026. Management can use that report to update investors on contracted GPU capacity, utilization and any quantified contribution from new wins like Wayve.

stories.Headline: Apple plans to turn Siri into an AI agent with new iPhone updates: Report
stories.Summary:
Apple's new chief executive, John Ternus, is pressing software chief Craig Federighi to turn Siri into an AI agent that can take actions on its own and carry out a range of tasks for users, according to a report from Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. Gurman's reporting was covered by Mashable on November 9, 2026, and by The Tech Buzz the day before. Federighi's team shipped a working Siri AI on what insiders called an incredibly short timeline, but Apple executives privately admit the company is not keeping pace with rivals. The goal is an assistant that can compete with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse.

Two upgrades are coming to Siri, according to Gurman's sources. The first gives the assistant more precise control over Apple's own apps, such as editing a photo in Photos and then sharing it with someone, rotating and cropping images, or organizing Safari tabs by topic. That part might arrive as early as December, with the public release of iOS 27.3, whose first beta Apple recently launched. The second upgrade lets Siri tap into third-party apps and act inside them, for example booking a table through OpenTable or ordering food through Uber Eats. Those capabilities are not expected until spring 2027, most likely with iOS 27.5 or iOS 27.6, with a possible launch ahead of Apple's WWDC conference in June.

Responsibility sits with Ternus and Federighi, whose relationship Bloomberg describes in detail. Federighi is portrayed as an AI skeptic, while Ternus pushes for a more progressive approach to AI. Mashable says Siri AI is far more capable than last year's Siri but still cannot take a pile of complex tasks and return results. Even with the coming upgrades, Mashable adds, Siri would not match agents like ChatGPT's Dots or Meta's Muse, which can be given a job such as building a website and then work through its steps while improving the project. Gurman believes Apple intends to launch comparable capabilities as early as next year.

The articles give some background on how Apple reached this point. Siri was an early success for the company but in recent years became a pain point as it lagged behind large language models such as OpenAI's ChatGPT. Apple improved it significantly this year and rebranded the whole system Siri AI. One agent-style feature was already announced at WWDC 2026, which lets Siri find weak passwords tied to a user's Apple account and change them autonomously on the relevant websites and in the Passwords app. Apple also recently began integrating ChatGPT support into its HomeView smart hub, a sign that it is willing to lean on a rival where its own technology falls short.

The competitive picture is moving quickly, according to The Tech Buzz. OpenAI just closed an $11 billion funding round that values the company at $1.25 trillion, and its Dots agent can handle tasks like booking travel and managing schedules. Meta has been rolling out Muse across its family of apps, and Amazon launched a text-to-shop Alexa feature after blocking Muse from its platform. Gurman argues Apple can afford to be a bit more cautious because it controls both the hardware and software of its devices, though rivals could start developing hardware of their own, which could erode Apple's most important market advantage. The Tech Buzz adds that it remains unclear whether Apple can compress its development timeline enough to matter.

stories.Headline: Anthropic Goes for Microsoft’s Crown With New Claude-Powered Office Tools
stories.Summary:
On Tuesday, November 10, 2026, Anthropic unveiled a set of AI-powered office tools at an event in San Francisco. Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets launched in beta, and Claude Dashboards, which had entered beta in October, became generally available under the new name Claude Data. The Verge reported a third tool, Claude Meetings, that can join a meeting, take notes and turn a presentation into a one-minute explainer video, while Gizmodo said it is coming soon. Whiteboards and Sheets are open to all paid plans, and The Verge said Meetings will be available to Teams and Enterprise subscriptions. The company also introduced interactive connectors that open partner apps inside Claude.

Anthropic describes Whiteboards as a shared board where a team brainstorms with Claude, which can turn a spoken, messy plan into a timeline with owners and dates. In a retro meeting, for example, everyone can add notes, and Claude can group them by theme and draft action items for each person. Sheets lets Claude build and edit spreadsheets with tabs, formulas, formatting and drop-downs, often from a single prompt such as a request for a campaign tracker or hiring budget. It outlines each edit so changes can be tracked, and for now it offers only simple spreadsheet functionality, with more planned. Files can be exported to .xlsx or CSV, used through Claude for Excel, or continued in partner tools including Airtable, Asana, monday.com and Smartsheet.

Claude Data lets teams ask questions of company data held in tools like Amazon Redshift, BigQuery and ClickHouse. A data team can certify queries so that charts built on them carry a certified badge, and certified queries and live sharing are both in beta. With live sharing, colleagues see current numbers even without access to the underlying connectors, but they can only view the results of approved queries. The product also now supports design systems, caching with per-dashboard refresh cadences, and tracked changes with rollback to a specific version. Named partners include Amplitude, Mixpanel, Omni, PostHog and Sigma.

For administrators, all three tools are on by default on Team plans. On Enterprise plans, Whiteboards and Sheets are off by default, while Claude Data switches on by default on November 19, 2026. Settings can be changed under Organization settings > Artifacts. The tools work on web, desktop and mobile, and Claude Data requires a data connector such as a warehouse or CRM. The interactive connectors let apps from companies including Adobe, Atlassian, Box and Notion open beside a conversation or in full screen.

Nicholas Lin, who works on product at Anthropic, told The Verge that Claude Code changed how engineers work a year ago and that knowledge workers are now the gap the company hopes to close. He said there is still a lot of friction in adopting AI for non-developers. Lin added that Claude Cowork, another tool for non-engineers, is essentially a wrapper for Claude Code aimed at the technical parts of Anthropic's non-technical audience. Anthropic said in its own announcement that its aim is to keep documents, boards, sheets and dashboards inside Claude so teams can keep editing together. Gizmodo's Ece Yildirim called Sheets the most direct threat to Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets, noting it works almost exactly like those apps.

The new tools join existing ones such as Claude Docs, Slides, Design and Motion, and arrive two and a half years after Artifacts first debuted. Lin said Anthropic launched Model Context Protocol about two years ago and its marketplace has grown to more than 9,000 plugin options, and the company now wants those connections to be deeper. The Verge noted that Google's Gemini and, in some cases, OpenAI's ChatGPT can already join meetings and take live notes. It also said Anthropic faces pressure to generate revenue ahead of an IPO that could be the most valuable public debut ever, with a separate headline citing a $1.4 trillion target. Gizmodo reported that the company is reportedly looking to debut on the stock market on November 19, despite jitters around the broader AI industry, and that the Nasdaq had its worst month in over a year last month.

stories.Headline: AMD Showcases 6th Gen AMD EPYC Processors to Lead Next Era of AI and Enterprise Computing
stories.Summary:
AMD announced on November 10, 2026 from Santa Clara, California that its 6th Gen EPYC SP7 server processors, built on the new Zen 6 architecture, are now generally available. Systems based on the chips are already shipping from leading server makers, and cloud instances from Microsoft Azure and OCI are due to become generally available soon. The chips are expected to power cloud instances across all major global cloud providers. A day later, on November 11, 2026, Super Micro Computer said its H15 generation server portfolio, powered by the 6th Gen EPYC 9006 Series processors, formerly codenamed Venice, is also shipping.

AMD says the 6th Gen EPYC range spans agentic AI, enterprise, cloud computing, HPC and general-purpose computing. Its EPYC 9996 CPU is described as the world's best general-purpose processor, with up to 3.7 times the performance of a system based on Nvidia's Vera CPU. Against an Intel Xeon 6980P system, AMD claims up to 2.2 times the performance and 2.0 times the performance per dollar. High-frequency host-node processors reaching up to 5.3 GHz are said to deliver up to 1.8 times the LLM output throughput of the previous EPYC generation. AMD also claims its high-density chips offer roughly 3.3 times the agents per CPU watt of Nvidia Vera and about 2.5 times that of the Xeon 6980P when hosting agent sandboxes.

For racks, AMD says EPYC 9996 servers can support an estimated 1.18 times as many agents within the same 35 kilowatt power envelope as systems using default power-management settings. The processors also extend to AMD Helion agentic AI racks in three versions. Helion Liquid is meant to sit alongside the Helios rack-scale solution in large agentic AI deployments, Helion Air targets existing air-cooled data centers, and Helion Air Inference combines CPU execution with local GPU inference in one rack. Some Helion configurations reach up to 73,728 threads in a single rack.

Supermicro says its H15 platforms offer up to 33% more cores, twice the PCIe bandwidth, and 1.6 TB/s of memory bandwidth per socket. In one passage it also cites 2.6 times higher memory bandwidth, and it claims 1.8 times higher tokens per second for frontier-model host nodes than previous AMD CPU generations. The company reports multiple SPEC CPU world records on its 2U Hyper and CloudDC servers. Its portfolio of more than 20 systems includes Hyper, CloudDC, FlexTwin, GrandTwin, Petascale Storage with up to 4.8 PB per system, and SuperBlade, spanning AMD EPYC 9006 SP7 and SP8 socket servers. Supermicro is also bringing Helios, built around AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs, and Helion to market on its DCBBS architecture.

Dan McNamara, AMD's senior vice president and general manager for Compute and Enterprise AI, said AI is greatly widening the CPU's role across the data center. He said customers can stay on the proven x86 foundation while choosing workload-optimized chips to run more agents and keep accelerated infrastructure fed. Speaking about the Supermicro systems, he said the platforms help organizations deploy AI infrastructure faster, improve utilization, cut energy use and lower total cost of ownership. Michael McNerney, Supermicro's senior vice president of marketing, said the shipping H15 line gives customers a faster, more efficient route to agentic AI infrastructure. He credited close engineering work with AMD for the flexibility to scale AI, cloud and enterprise workloads.

AMD notes that across five generations EPYC processors have repeatedly raised the standard for server CPU performance, energy efficiency and platform choice. Its 5th Gen EPYC became the fastest-ramping and highest-volume EPYC generation in the company's history. AMD describes agentic AI as adding diversity to the data center, since one workflow can run agents, call models, retrieve data and execute code. It says Meta is working with AMD as a lead customer and has been validating 6th Gen EPYC platforms as the companies prepare for deployment at scale. Microsoft Azure is also bringing the processors to customers, and AMD has separately launched 6th Gen EPYC Embedded processors.

stories.Headline: Data Doctors: Can I trust AI shopping agents?
stories.Summary:
Zoho Corporation announced on November 10, 2026, that it is turning Zoho Analytics into what it calls an Agentic Analytics platform, adding a layer meant to give AI agents trusted business data and context. The company said the platform brings together data, analytics and AI agents so businesses can move from studying numbers to acting on them. A central feature is Ask Zia, a conversational assistant that now uses several specialized sub-agents working together. Zoho made the announcement from Singapore through the Media OutReach Newswire.

The update includes native semantic and ontology layers, which act as a business glossary and a map of how a company's entities relate to one another. Ask Zia has six pre-built sub-agents covering data analysis, visualization, data preparation, modeling, coding and SQL generation, and companies can use Zoho's own language model or bring their own. Teams can also build custom agents that connect to outside tools through the Model Context Protocol. Zoho added more than 30 new data connectors to the 500-plus it already offered, including ones for SAP, PayPal, Adobe Commerce, Twilio and Notion, along with more than 50 other new capabilities. Pricing is unchanged, and every plan now includes Zoho LLM credits, with a Basic plan starting at US$24 per month billed annually, covering 2 users, 0.5 million rows and 10K credits.

Gibu Mathew, Managing Director of Zoho APAC, said agents cannot work on data alone and need a solid intelligence layer, which he said the update provides. He described it as one open and extensible layer that gives every AI tool in a business the context, metrics and governance to produce answers people can rely on. Zoho also stressed oversight features, such as a data catalog, AI usage and cost tracking, and a sandbox for testing agents before publishing them. The company said Zoho Analytics is used by 100,000 businesses worldwide daily.

Zoho said the cloud version of the updates is available now, with some preview versions still to arrive. It plans to expand the designed context into a dynamic one that tracks how business data changes over time, add decision intelligence based on the actions agents trigger, and keep investing in open standards, including the Apache Ossie specification. It also plans to build Zoho Analytics into a fuller unified data platform that would include a data lakehouse. Separately, a Quartz report on AI shopping agents says Meta's Muse agent was downloaded 10 million times in the U.S. within 40 days of its early September launch, with purchases averaging more than $200. It adds that agentic web traffic roughly tripled from August to September and that Amazon blocked Muse soon after launch, while the other shopping article supplied no readable text.

stories.Headline: Paras Semiconductors partners with US firm BroadPak for advanced chip packaging in India
stories.Summary:
Paras Semiconductors, a subsidiary of Paras Defence and Space Technologies, has announced a technology partnership with US-based BroadPak Corporation to develop advanced semiconductor packaging capabilities in India. The announcement came in a release on Monday, November 10, 2026, and was reported from New Delhi. Through the tie-up, Paras Semiconductors aims to set up an advanced heterogeneous integration and 3D packaging OSAT facility in the country. OSAT stands for outsourced semiconductor assembly and test.

The proposed unit will focus on 2.5D/3D packaging, chiplet integration, hybrid bonding, wafer-level and panel-level fan-out packaging, co-packaged optics, and testing and qualification. Paras Semiconductors will gain access to BroadPak's design, manufacturing and integration intellectual property, along with technology transfer and process know-how. The planned manufacturing unit will also incorporate through-silicon vias, micro-bumping, advanced interposers and redistribution layer technologies, along with wafer-level processing and reliability testing. The two firms will also explore joint development of packaging platforms for AI and high-performance computing applications. They plan to collaborate as well on training and skill development programmes for Indian engineers.

The facility is meant to serve high-volume manufacturing and strategic electronics needs, including devices for optical and optronic systems, high-performance computing, networking and data centres. Munjal Sharad Shah, Managing Director of Paras Defence and Space Technologies, described the move into semiconductors as a strategic expansion into a technology domain that is increasingly critical to India's AI, data centre and industrial capabilities. He said the collaboration would help build packaging capabilities that complement the company's existing strengths in optics, optronics and critical electronics. He added that the initiative would address India's strategic domestic requirements as well as the wider needs of the semiconductor industry.

Santosh Kumar, CEO of Paras Semiconductors, said the company intends to build a packaging platform that can meet the performance, connectivity and thermal needs of next-generation applications. He said the collaboration would support capabilities in heterogeneous integration, chiplet architectures, hybrid bonding and advanced system-in-package technologies. Farhang Yazdani, Founder and CEO of BroadPak, noted that India's growing semiconductor ecosystem offers an important opportunity to develop capabilities in heterogeneous integration and system-level packaging. He pointed in particular to rising demand for AI and high-performance computing.

BroadPak is headquartered in San Jose, California, and was founded in 2007. According to the release, it brings specialised expertise across advanced packaging design, manufacturing and system integration. Its capabilities cover 2.5D/3D IC packaging, heterogeneous integration, multi-die architectures, high-speed interconnects, thermal management and co-packaged optics. Growing demand for advanced packaging technologies, including chiplets, 2.5D/3D integration and hybrid bonding, strengthened the case for the collaboration. Through the partnership, Paras Semiconductors aims to strengthen its presence in India's domestic semiconductor packaging ecosystem and develop capabilities for emerging computing and strategic electronics applications.

stories.Headline: Prediction: This Could Be the Biggest AI Stock You’re Not Talking About
stories.Summary:
Micron Technology shares fell sharply this week, dropping 30.02% over the past week, 35.32% over the past month and 13.47% on the day the first article was written. The stock was at $688.09, which is 45.2% below its 52-week high of $1,254.61, though it is still up 141.28% year to date. The article says the selling also hit SanDisk and other AI names, and it ties the declines to market share concerns and a pause on a Taiwan plant after a labor dispute. A 24/7 Wall St. analysis nonetheless set a 12-month price target of $913.86 for Micron, which implies 32.8% upside and carries a buy signal with high confidence.

Micron just finished a fiscal year with $133.19B in revenue and $75.52 in non-GAAP EPS, yet the stock trades at roughly 9x trailing earnings and 4x forward EPS estimates. In fiscal Q4, revenue reached $54.23B against a $50.97B estimate, and non-GAAP EPS came in at $33.42 versus a $31.35 consensus, the company's eighth consecutive beat. Gross margin hit 87%. For fiscal Q1, management guided to $61.5B plus or minus $1.5B in revenue and $38.15 plus or minus $1.00 in EPS. The article says revenue grew 379% year over year.

On valuation, the article compares Micron with two peers. NVIDIA trades at 40x earnings with revenue growth of 105.85%, and the author says it commands a far higher multiple than Micron for slower growth. SanDisk, described as the closest memory peer, grew revenue 377.95% yet trades at 13x. The article says NVIDIA is Micron's most important HBM partner, with supply obligations of $279 billion largely tied to memory procurement for Vera Rubin. Against these peers, the author calls the 24/7 Wall St. target conservative.

Management said more than 75% of fiscal 2027 shipments are already committed, and Micron now has 26 Strategic Customer Agreements running through 2030. Executives called DRAM the principal constraint versus logic or power to the data center. Micron also raised HBM pricing for calendar 2027 and is co-designing HBM4E with NVIDIA. The analyst consensus target is $1,561.91, backed by 9 Strong Buy ratings and 36 Buy ratings, while the bull case of $1,342.01 implies 95.0% upside.

The article lists several risks. Memory has always been cyclical, fiscal 2026 capex reached $30.71B, and a large share of HBM sales goes to a small group of customers. The Taiwan plant pause and the market share questions add execution risk, and the bear case of $691.64 would leave the stock roughly flat for a year. Management will add equipment as demand requires, since most of the new construction budget goes to clean rooms for 2028, and free cash flow of $62.31B covers that spending easily. The author says the thesis strengthens if fiscal Q1 lands near guidance and more agreements are signed, and weakens if DRAM pricing rolls over or the Taiwan delay spreads to other projects.

A second article, from Motley Fool, covers a different stock, Upstart Holdings, which uses AI to judge borrower creditworthiness and originates loans for banks and other funding partners. Its stock has declined by 50% this year as of the Nov. 6 close, and it fell 8.27% to $20.41 on Nov. 10, with a 52-week range of $19.71 to $52.10. Writer Anthony Di Pizio predicts it will double over the next 12 months, and says rising interest rates are a short-term headwind. Upstart's model weighs more than 2,500 data points and was 2.77 times as accurate as traditional methods in the third quarter of 2026, a record high.

In that quarter Upstart approved a record 574,089 loans worth $4.1 billion, up 44% from a year earlier. The company said it could have grown faster without macroeconomic headwinds, and it has lowered its 2026 guidance while remaining on track for a record year. Home equity line of credit originations more than doubled year over year, and automotive loans more than tripled. Chairman Dave Girouard believes AI will replace all human-driven loan assessment within the next decade, leaving $25 trillion in annual global originations and $1 trillion in fee revenue up for grabs.

stories.Headline: Microsoft rejects multibillion-dollar AI deal with UK's Nscale
stories.Summary:
Microsoft has decided not to exercise an option to more than double the size of its existing agreement with Nscale, the London-based AI cloud provider, to rent computing power at a Texas data center. The Financial Times reported the news on Thursday, November 5, 2026, saying the extension would have been worth tens of billions of dollars to Nscale. A person familiar with the matter told Reuters that Microsoft made the decision several months ago, before Nscale filed for its IPO in September. The source said the existing Texas contract is not affected.

The option was part of a deal the two companies signed in October 2025, under which Nscale would supply about 200,000 Nvidia GB300 chips to Microsoft across sites in the US and Europe. Texas is the largest part of that arrangement, where Nscale leases a 240-megawatt campus in Barstow from the bitcoin miner Ionic Digital. It is due to deliver about 104,000 chips to Microsoft there from the third quarter of 2026. Nscale said at the time that Microsoft also held an option on a second, 700-megawatt phase at the site from late 2027. In its IPO filing, Nscale said it signed statements of work with Microsoft worth up to about $43.8 billion through December 2033, excluding optional extensions.

The source said that skipping the option has no effect on Nscale's total contract value of about $103 billion, as disclosed in the filing. Nscale was already in talks with several major customers for the remaining Texas capacity, the person added. Microsoft and Nscale did not respond to requests for comment outside business hours. Øyvind Eriksen, chief executive of Aker, the Norwegian group that owns about 23% of Nscale, had earlier played down a separate UK setback, calling that contract a relatively minor one in a bigger portfolio.

The news follows another blow to the partnership. Weeks earlier, Microsoft pulled out of a deal to anchor Nscale's flagship data center project in Loughton, Essex, billed as the UK's largest AI data center, after power connection delays pushed its expected supply date into the 2030s. Nscale, which counts Nvidia among its backers, is asking investors to value it at up to $35 billion in its New York listing, and it closed a $3.36 billion pre-IPO round before filing. Reuters and others reported last month that Nscale is also in talks to sell AI computing power to Anthropic, the maker of Claude, in a deal that could be worth about $45 billion.

stories.Headline: CoreWeave vs. Nebius: Which Is the Better AI Neocloud Stock to Own for the Next 3 Years?
stories.Summary:
CoreWeave jumped 5% on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, as AI stocks bounced back from the previous week's selloff, and Nebius rose 7% without any company news of its own. The Nasdaq 100 ETF gained 3% the same day. Both companies report this week, CoreWeave on Tuesday and Nebius on Thursday. The articles describe the sector as having had a rough month, with several neocloud stocks losing about half their market value. Last Thursday's declines also contributed to the Nasdaq's steepest daily fall in 19 months.

CoreWeave's balance sheet is at the center of the scrutiny. Its total debt, leases included, climbed to $51.6 billion at June 30 from $6.28 billion in September 2024. Management guided to $860 million to $940 million of third-quarter interest expense, against $200 million to $260 million of adjusted operating income. Another account puts cash at $5.5 billion against $35 billion in debt at the end of June, including $1.3 billion on a 15% facility due in March 2028 and $3.2 billion on an 11% facility due in August 2030. Analysts expect revenue to more than double this year to $12.9 billion and reach $43.7 billion by 2028, yet the stock traded at 1.3x forward sales at Friday's close, against a 3.5x average over the past year.

Credit markets have grown less forgiving. Yields on some CoreWeave bonds maturing in 2031 rose above 16%, and the spread on its five-year credit default swaps climbed above 1,240 basis points, up about 50% in a month. Nebius passed on a high-yield bond and took a $3.5 billion senior secured credit facility from Citigroup instead. IREN went another route, signing a five-year contract after its Sept. 30 quarter in which the customer prepays 90% of the GPU capex. IREN carries $10 billion in debt, and about 48% of its backlog is tied to Microsoft, yet its shares rebounded 20% on Friday after it said AI cloud revenue had more than doubled.

Commentators offered differing readings of the move and the risks. TIKR's author credited the sector for Monday's gains and said he would not read much into the bounce. If interest expense tops the guide, he expects the gain to vanish, while adjusted operating income at the top of the guide could send the stock a lot higher. NYU Stern professor Scott Galloway called the neocloud companies "levered trades to AI." Morningstar analyst Luke Yang said CoreWeave appears able to fulfil its existing contracts and is unlikely to face bankruptcy soon, but that a depressed stock price makes equity financing unattractive and he wants to hear how management plans to close the financing gap.

Paul Meeks of Freedom Capital Markets called the situation a self-fulfilling "doom cycle," in which worried creditors force CoreWeave to borrow at steep rates to fund its buildout. He noted that CoreWeave generated $5 billion in revenue in 2025 and estimated it could reach $42 billion by 2028 with an EBITDA margin approaching 70%. Partners Group's Anastasia Amoroso said neoclouds would be the most affected by the deterioration in conditions. IREN co-chief executive Daniel Roberts said there is a disconnect between public markets and what he sees at the customer level, and that capital markets now ask whether a contract can be delivered, financed and run at a profit. CoreWeave chief executive Mike Intrator said he did not expect political shifts to affect existing customer commitments or the contracted backlog.

Politics has added to the uncertainty. Democratic candidates won gubernatorial races in Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas last week, and voters rejected data center proposals in all but one of 41 related ballot measures across the United States. In October, Applied Digital, CoreWeave's landlord in North Dakota, signed a memorandum of understanding to assign one building's lease to a CoreWeave subsidiary if that subsidiary wins an investment-grade rating. Unlike Amazon and Microsoft, the leading neocloud companies remain unprofitable and rely on a small group of customers. Nscale filed for an IPO in September but has not published an updated prospectus, SB Energy faces similar uncertainty, and Firmus abandoned its IPO plans last month.

stories.Headline: Putting AI on pause: South Portland schools consider moratorium
stories.Summary:
On Nov. 9, 2026, the South Portland School Board voted down a proposed moratorium on student-facing generative artificial intelligence for the remainder of the 2026-2027 school year. The vote was 6-1, and the only member in favor was At-Large Board Member Claire Holman, who had proposed the measure. The board took up the question at its regular meeting, which began at 6 p.m. with the proposal on the agenda. After the vote, the South Portland School Department remained without a specific AI policy.

According to official city documents, the moratorium would have paused student-facing generative AI use in classrooms and assignments for students in grades PreK-8 across the district. The pause was meant to give the board time to develop an appropriate AI policy. The proposal also said the school department would make sure all staff received two hours of AI awareness training and three hours of AI literacy training. After that training, teachers would have been allowed to use only AI tools sanctioned by the South Portland School Department, though they would not have been required to use AI. Exceptions could have covered assistive technologies and centrally approved instructional uses.

Several community members spoke against the proposal during public comment. Peter Wetzel, a middle school computer science teacher and South Portland resident, said it was the first time he had heard about the moratorium and that it would directly affect a curriculum he had worked hard to build. Cidney Mayes, a fifth- and sixth-grade digital literacy teacher at South Portland Middle School, said AI literacy makes up a significant portion of her curriculum and that she would lose four weeks of instruction if the moratorium passed. Some speakers backed the idea, including one who said AI use can weaken children's critical thinking, and the mother of a kindergartner at Frank I. Brown Elementary School, who supported the resolution but asked for exceptions for classes that teach AI literacy. Ian Archibald, a South Portland High School student, said some teachers use AI in their courses and that it had lowered his learning experience.

Holman said the proposal did not stop students from learning about AI and did not bar teachers from using it to build their curriculum. She asked what would happen if the district's children could not think, and said she simply did not like AI. Board Vice Chair Tyler Smith and At-Large Board Member Eleni Richardson spoke against the moratorium, with Richardson saying many high school students she had spoken with are not excited about AI. Board Chair Rosemarie DeAngelis said she would not support the moratorium and wanted to wait for a more detailed plan, and Superintendent Dr. Angela Atkinson Duina said she was confident in the judgment and oversight of the district's educators.

Student Representative Sarah Lupien told the board that AI had not negatively affected her learning, noting that many of her classes never discuss it, and that she trusts her teachers to make informed choices about its use. After the vote, Mayes returned to the podium to thank the board and said something was wrong if she had to justify her curriculum. A teacher from Waldo T. Skillin Elementary School criticized the lack of teacher consultation while the proposal was being written. WGME reported that board members said the conversation is far from over, and that officials are now working on a comprehensive plan set to launch in January. That plan is meant to address AI integration as well as broader cybersecurity issues in the district.

stories.Headline: Senator tells Google to let US schools disable AI features in search
stories.Summary:
US Senator Ed Markey sent a letter to Google on Nov 9 telling the company to let schools disable the artificial intelligence features within its search engine. The Massachusetts Democrat addressed it to Alphabet chief executive Sundar Pichai, and he said schools should not have to choose between enabling AI tools and keeping Google Search. The letter followed a New York Times report that Google planned to turn off student access to certain AI-related services, including its Gemini tool and search, giving schools the option of turning any back on. Google said schools cannot switch off AI features in search if they want to keep using it to run queries, because tools like AI Overview and AI Mode are too deeply integrated into search. AI Mode is a chatbot-like feature, while AI Overview generates search summaries.

In his letter, Markey asked Google whether it would change course and let schools disable student access to the AI features within search without losing the search engine. He also asked whether it was technically feasible to give K-12 students logged into their school Google accounts search results that did not include AI-generated responses or guidance. He requested any research the company had conducted on the safety and learning effects of AI features in search, with the deadline reported as the end of the month, and one article gives it as Nov 30. He also wants to know whether schools can disable AI Overviews, Gemini and Guided Learning while keeping Google Search. In addition, he asked how the company evaluates the risks of students' access to AI tools and what safeguards schools have.

Markey said Google was using its dominant position in the education technology sector to push AI chatbots onto children and teenagers, whether or not their schools believe the technology is safe. He called the arrangement an ultimatum rather than a choice, one that effectively forces schools to enable generative AI. Google said its changes would make it easier for schools to control student access to AI. The company also announced a new student AI chat feature called Guided Learning, which it says helps students work through questions rather than simply provide answers and is meant to tamp down on AI cheating. Google education executive Chris Phillips announced in a Nov 3 blog post that Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Google Search would stay disabled for K-12 accounts until administrators explicitly activated them.

Google's announcement drew criticism from some politicians and nonprofit groups, who said its insistence on keeping AI features in search undermined schools' ability to make learning and safety decisions for their students. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani also criticised the approach, accusing the company of using its market position to encourage public schools to adopt AI services. Markey cited a lawsuit alleging that Gemini helped a minor develop a suicide plan, and according to his letter the student reached the chatbot through Google Search on a school-issued Chromebook despite restrictions on its standalone services. The allegations have not been established in court. A Google spokesperson told CBS News that AI features are closely integrated with Search, so the company cannot offer the search service separately from them.

The tech industry is facing heightened public concern that chatbots can hinder students' learning and pose risks to children's mental health. Markey's letter also cited an August Times story reporting that Google had turned on AI features in Google Classroom, a schoolwork assignment app, for K-12 students in schools that had enabled its Gemini chatbot. Google now plans to turn those features off. A limited pilot programme involving US schools is scheduled to begin later in November, and Google has not said whether it will revise its policy in response to the senator's request.

stories.Headline: New York's AI Safety Law Hits OpenAI, Anthropic Today
stories.Summary:
New York State opened a corporate registration portal on November 10 ahead of the implementation of its RAISE Act, an AI safety and transparency law aimed at frontier AI developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic. One report framed the law as taking effect that day and forcing the two companies to register with regulators, disclose their safety practices and report critical incidents or face financial penalties. A second report said the act itself takes effect early next year. Governor Kathy Hochul signed the bill into law earlier this year.

The law covers frontier AI developers with annual revenues above $500 million, and those companies must register with state authorities by January 1, 2027. They must publicly disclose their safety management systems on their websites, detailing how they identify and manage AI risks, and must issue model transparency reports. Major safety incidents must be reported to authorities within 72 hours, with a preliminary assessment. One report said registration calls for detailed filings on model architectures, training data sources, safety testing protocols and incident response procedures.

Enforcement falls to a newly established agency, the Division of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity and Trust, known as DIGIT, which oversees large AI research labs and checks compliance with the statutory safety obligations. Penalties run up to $1 million for a first violation and up to $3 million for later violations. State authorities said they can take enforcement action against unregistered companies as well, but did not disclose how. One report said the exact fine structure remained under regulatory review, and that the agency had not said how many investigators it has assigned to AI oversight or what its audit schedule looks like.

The law defines a critical incident broadly, as any malfunction, misuse or unexpected behavior that results in significant harm to individuals, critical infrastructure or public safety. One report said that could cover a chatbot giving dangerous medical advice or an AI system being used for large-scale misinformation campaigns. The same report said the ambiguity is intentional, giving regulators flexibility as new risks emerge. It also said the law targets "advanced AI systems," meaning models with broad capabilities across multiple domains that could pose systemic risks.

Hochul also launched the New York AI Responsibility and Research Center at Binghamton University, part of SUNY, on the same day. The center will independently assess whether advanced AI systems operate safely, examine security and operational methods, and review corporate safety policies together with DIGIT. Hochul first announced plans for the center in January, backed by $55 million in donations and capital. Speaking at a briefing, she criticized tech companies for justifying harm in the name of the AI development race, and said the state is building a regulatory model that puts communities before corporations and people before powerful technology.

The timing falls close to major moves at both companies. Anthropic priced its IPO at $70 to $78 per share ahead of its November 19 public debut, and launched Claude Meetings and shipped new Mythos and Fable models this week. OpenAI recently turned ChatGPT into a business discovery engine, letting companies create profiles and listings inside the chatbot. Neither company had issued a public statement about the New York deadline, though both have previously expressed support for "thoughtful regulation" in congressional testimony. Lobbyists were reported to be working to shape implementation details and to push for federal preemption of state laws.

The reports place the law alongside other state measures. California's SB 53, which took effect in January, requires frontier developers to establish and disclose safety policies and protect whistleblowers, and mandates reporting of major incidents within 15 days. Illinois's SB 315 takes effect early next year and adds independent audits of compliance with safety standards. Colorado and Massachusetts have working groups studying the issue, while California's legislature debated similar measures earlier this year but did not adopt comprehensive AI regulation. The federal government has not enacted comprehensive AI safety rules, and one report predicted copycat legislation across blue states by mid-2027 if New York's enforcement goes smoothly.

stories.Headline: Quantinuum and RIKEN Expand Partnership to Accelerate the Commercialization of Quantum-AI Hybrid Supercomputing in Japan
stories.Summary:
Quantinuum announced on November 10, 2026 that its Reimei quantum computer at the Riken supercomputing center in Japan has been upgraded to the company's 56-qubit System Model H2. The company confirmed the upgrade in an 8-K press release alongside an expanded partnership with Riken and SoftBank Corp. Reimei sits at Riken in Wako, Saitama, and is operated as part of the JHPC-quantum project, which is funded by NEDO, the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization, an organization under Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry. The earlier H1 version of the system went in during February 2025 with 20 qubits, and it was Quantinuum's first on-premise delivery of a system. The upgraded machine is described as boosting the quantum-HPC hybrid computing platform and letting researchers explore complex quantum systems that are hard to simulate on classical computers alone.

The expanded deal with Riken rests on a Memorandum of Understanding aimed at advanced scientific and industrial applications. Under it, the partners will work with Japanese universities and domestic component suppliers toward a "Made with Japan" fault-tolerant quantum computer. That effort will combine Quantinuum's quantum technology with domestic research and manufacturing expertise, and it will draw on what was learned deploying and operating Reimei at Riken. Under a separate agreement, Quantinuum, Riken and SoftBank will explore connecting quantum computing directly with AI data centers in Japan. The three will assess infrastructure readiness and examine how connected systems could support commercial quantum-AI hybrid computing services.

Two research projects are already running on the upgraded Reimei platform. One combines Riken's ROQUO GPU supercomputer with quantum data from Reimei to train an AI model for magnetism simulations, and early results indicate the model can give more precise predictions than AI models trained only on classical simulations. The other links Reimei, Riken's Fugaku supercomputer and an NVIDIA evolutionary AI agent running on ROQUO to simulate a complex photoactive biomolecule. The filing says a better grasp of how such biomolecules respond to light could drive more efficient solar cells and other industrial applications. It also says the research aligns with a planned $1 billion partnership under the U.S. Genesis Mission.

Quantinuum chief executive Rajeeb Hazra said Japan's quantum ambitions call for advanced capabilities today and a sustained commitment to what comes next. He said the Reimei upgrade widens what can be explored with Riken across electronics, energy and life sciences. Hazra added that the company is building toward a fault-tolerant machine with Japanese universities and suppliers while exploring with SoftBank how these capabilities can reach industry through Japan's AI data centers. Takenori Kobayashi, vice president and head of the product research and development division at SoftBank Corp., said Japan has built a strong base for hybrid quantum-HPC computing through the NEDO-supported JHPC-quantum project. He said SoftBank's responsibility is to turn those achievements into industrial value, aiming for a Quantum AI Datacenter that connects quantum computing with AI and HPC for businesses across Japan.

Quantinuum was founded in 2021 when Honeywell spun out its Quantum Solutions division and merged it with the UK startup Cambridge Quantum Computing. Honeywell holds a 54 percent stake in the company, and IBM is also an investor. The filing says Quantinuum has about 800 employees worldwide, with more than 70 percent of its technology team holding PhDs or Master's degrees. Quantum computers were once confined to custom spaces at company labs and supercomputing centers, but they are increasingly being placed in commercial data centers and linked to classical GPU- and CPU-powered supercomputers.

stories.Headline: Trust Stamp launches biometric approval tool for AI-agent transactions
stories.Summary:
Trust Stamp, which trades on the Nasdaq as IDAI, announced on November 10, 2026 a new product that confirms a bank customer knowingly approves each transaction that an AI agent initiates on their behalf. The Atlanta-based company calls the product Knowing Consent. It relies on proprietary processes protected by existing issued patents, together with a new process that is being patented, and the company says it is ready for immediate use. The announcement was distributed through GlobeNewswire and reported by Proactive Investors.

The authorization flow can be started either by the AI agent or by the financial institution. On first use, the customer completes biometric registration to create a personal identity token. For later requests, the customer can be prompted to take a secure selfie through SMS, email, push notification or the relevant software application. Proof-of-life and anti-spoofing checks, with optional device verification and other authentication protocols, confirm the account owner is present when approval is requested. In an integrated deployment, the authorization screen should show the specific action and its details before the customer completes the live verification, so the fresh approval is tied to that request.

Chief executive Gareth N. Genner said the approach reflects the need for controls at the moment an AI agent acts. He said Trust Stamp has over one hundred financial institutions integrated to its Orchestration Layer, and that the tool adds a live, customer-centered approval step to agent-initiated activity. According to Genner, it can be put in place in a matter of days, either through the Orchestration Layer or a single API call. He added that it runs within an institution's own access and transaction policies, with no significant changes to its authentication flow, and contrasted it with Agent-Identity proposals in the media, which he called theoretical, while saying these human-centered processes already exist and are proven to be effective.

On November 11, 2026, the company announced that Provisional Patent number 64/195,409 was issued by the United States Patent and Trademark Office on November 9, 2026. That filing, together with the existing issued patents, protects the Knowing Consent product. Genner commented that this human-centric utility is ready to use, unlike the various Agent-Identity concepts being proposed in the media. He repeated that more than one hundred banks are already integrated to the Orchestration Layer.

The company framed the launch around a problem banks now face: when an agent uses a customer's credentials, a bank has difficulty telling the customer's present intent from the agent's actions. Trust Stamp cited a NIST Cybersecurity Insights article in which Bill Fisher and Ryan Galluzzo wrote that credential sharing is a bad idea in all contexts and can create accountability gaps. It also pointed to a Reuters report that major U.S. banks are blocking some third-party agents from customer accounts. JPMorgan Chase chief executive Jamie Dimon described unrestricted outside agents as too risky for clients and for the bank, and JPMorganChase has said agent safeguards must operate at the point of execution. RBC has blocked direct access of third-party agents to authenticated online banking, saying such agents may store customer passwords.

The company says the distinction matters when an agent has been given broad access in advance, or when its behavior is changed by error or manipulation. It argues that a stored password or earlier permission should not by itself be treated as proof that the customer knowingly approved a particular financial action. Trust Stamp describes its approach as human-centered, identifying the customer and ensuring that they give consent, rather than identifying AI agents. More information and the company's Knowing Consent whitepaper are available on its website.

stories.Headline: FuelCell Energy to develop AI data center power testbed in Danbury
stories.Summary:
FuelCell Energy said on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that it is taking part in StabilityMax, a three-year project led by the U.S. Department of Energy's National Laboratory of the Rockies in Golden, Colorado. Argonne National Laboratory is also participating. As part of the work, the company will build a federally backed testbed in Danbury, Connecticut, where it is headquartered. The project will study how fuel cells, batteries and power electronics can work together to provide reliable power to AI data centers. Their electricity consumption changes rapidly, which can strain utility grids.

The testbed will have a capacity of 1.25 megawatts and will be built at a Danbury site that has not yet been chosen. Company spokeswoman Kathleen Blomquist said FuelCell has not set a date for it to begin operating. She said the company is not disclosing the project's cost or how much federal funding is involved, though FuelCell will supply the fuel cell and related technology. The project will not add jobs beyond engineering positions the company is already recruiting for, she said. The company says the facility will let it evaluate integrated power solutions under realistic conditions and optimize system design and performance.

The two national laboratories have separate roles. The National Laboratory of the Rockies will develop data center power-demand profiles and simulation models to test FuelCell's technology under realistic operating conditions. Argonne will carry out cost and lifecycle analyses to identify commercially viable ways to deploy the systems. Zhiwen Ma, the Rockies lab's principal investigator, said the project will help show how integrated fuel cell systems can respond rapidly to data center power needs while limiting impacts on the utility grid and ratepayers. Shankar Achanta, FuelCell's chief product and technology officer, said AI infrastructure is creating unprecedented demand for reliable, flexible and resilient power.

The project comes as FuelCell expands its manufacturing capacity and pursues a growing pipeline of data center customers. In June, the company said it expects to spend $200 million to $275 million over about two years to expand its Torrington plant to 500 megawatts of annual production capacity. Its pipeline of potential data center projects has grown to about 10 gigawatts, according to earlier reporting by the Hartford Business Journal. A major data center operator has also made an upfront payment to reserve equipment for a planned 75-megawatt project in Texas. Earlier this year, FuelCell announced a collaboration with Siemens on power systems for AI data centers.

stories.Headline: Chinese university buys Nvidia AI H200 chips despite US ban, records show
stories.Summary:
A Chinese university with ties to the army bought Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips last month even though it sits on a US export blacklist. Northwestern Polytechnical University, a member of China's "Seven Sons of National Defense" group of elite defence-focused universities, bought two H200 chips for 874,700 yuan, or $123,000. The purchase appears in an October 21 procurement record on the university's website, which the Reuters news agency reported on. The chips were bought for the university's management school from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology, not directly from Nvidia. The university also bought access this year to H200 chips and other powerful Nvidia processors through five contracts for rented computing capacity from Chinese companies.

The H200 is among Nvidia's most capable chips for training and running advanced AI systems, and it requires US export licence approval. Those licences are normally denied for blacklisted institutions such as Northwestern Polytechnical. The Department of Commerce added the university to its Entity List in 2001 over alleged involvement in missile-proliferation activities and its military research. Washington tightened the restrictions in 2019, making licences for exporting controlled US technology to the university subject to a policy of denial in most circumstances. The university is based in the northwestern city of Xi'an and conducts research related to military aircraft, missiles and satellites.

A Reuters review of 26 Chinese procurement and corporate records from this year found universities and research institutions buying US-restricted Nvidia chips or renting access to computing services that use them. The suppliers in these cases were domestic Chinese firms, and several of the buyers had close links to China's defence industry or military research. US President Donald Trump's administration began allowing some H200 exports to China on a case-by-case basis in January. That policy did not lift the separate restrictions applying to Entity List organisations such as Northwestern Polytechnical. Both Democrats and Republicans in Congress have urged stronger controls, including chip-tracking requirements and greater congressional oversight of exports.

The Reuters investigation comes as Nvidia and its CEO Jensen Huang face mounting scrutiny in Washington over his lobbying for looser restrictions on AI chip sales to China. Huang has argued that continued US sales would preserve American technological leadership and keep Chinese customers reliant on Nvidia technology. Some US lawmakers counter that access to the most powerful chips can speed China's development of AI systems for weapons design, intelligence analysis and military modernisation. Republican Senator Kevin Cramer of the Senate Banking Committee told Politico that Huang should step down, citing the potential for extortion given the sensitivity of Nvidia chips.

Three Republican congressional committee chairmen have requested a briefing with Huang on November 18 over his reported contacts with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. The scrutiny stems from Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, who is accused of working for Chinese intelligence. Huang, who cofounded Nvidia more than three decades ago, admitted on Sunday to being unfaithful to his wife. The company said it has no reason to believe US national security or confidential information has been compromised, and its board announced an independent investigation into whether the 63-year-old had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

Alice Huang is a former executive at a Singapore-based data centre company. According to reports by Reuters, The Information and other outlets, she built a business structure linking China, Singapore and Malaysia with the help of Kang Wei, known as her husband, and her younger sister Huang Yu, though the New York Times said it could not confirm that she and Kang Wei were married. The companies involved include Shanghai Century Litong, launched in China in June 2023, the Singapore entity Megaspeed, and Megaspeed's Malaysian subsidiary SpeedMatrix. Century Litong, in which Huang Yu was a founding shareholder, won preferred Nvidia cloud partner status just four months after its establishment and received priority chip supplies.

The chips she smuggled into China or provided as leased data center computing resources are estimated at about 240,000 units, including H100, H200 and A100 processors, and were reportedly used to train models at Alibaba and Tencent as well as smaller Chinese AI companies. The operation drew the attention of the US Commerce Department, and an official found Nvidia equipment still in unopened packaging at a Megaspeed data center. Singapore authorities summoned her over suspicions of false import declarations but closed the investigation for lack of evidence. She later left for Shanghai, but Megaspeed's business continues, and figures linked to her have reportedly pressed ahead with data center construction in Malaysia.

stories.Headline: As AI stakes its claim in higher education, colleges and universities across Chicago aim to embrace it
stories.Summary:
DePaul University released a document called "Guiding Principles on Artificial Intelligence" last month, calling for academic integrity, intellectual honesty, transparency and human-centered use of the technology. The principles came out of the school's 26-member Provost's Advisory Committee on Artificial Intelligence, which worked for more than a year to develop them. The committee meets monthly to discuss policy, practices and how AI is used in the classroom. The Chicago Tribune reported the story on November 10, 2026, in a piece by Kate Perez.

The principles go beyond academic integrity, according to Jay Cunningham, an assistant professor of computing who created the Responsible AI Systems and Experiences, or RAISE, Lab, which he launched in 2025. About a dozen students routinely work at the lab on DePaul's Loop campus, exploring how AI affects daily life. Cunningham wants students to understand that AI is a tool that attempts to model human behavior, human interactions and human decision-making. Over the past half-decade, he has seen more fields demand that workers understand AI, which creates a need for students to learn the technology as it progresses.

Other Chicago campuses are making similar efforts, forming committees, launching AI classes and majors, and pushing for AI literacy among students and faculty. At the University of Chicago, a new master's degree in applied AI will launch in fall 2027, while the law school prohibits note-taking on electronic devices in some classes. This fall, Northwestern University launched an undergraduate major in AI and a webpage of tools and resources meant to help students, faculty and staff use generative AI effectively and responsibly. City Colleges of Chicago, which serves more than 73,000 students a year through its network of public community colleges, introduced its first AI degree program at Wilbur Wright College this fall. Students there can now earn an Associate of Applied Science degree in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Development.

John Shanahan, a professor of English and associate provost at DePaul, chairs the Advisory Committee on Artificial Intelligence. He said some faculty colleagues worried about AI's implications for higher education while others thrived with the new technology, and he brought them together. The committee created a shared space for faculty across disciplines, from acting to computer science, to talk about AI. Shanahan described its purpose as getting a sense of what is happening in the units, provoking discussion about what faculty hear from students, and vetting good ideas about what the university should do next.

Mark Potter, provost and chief academic officer of City Colleges, told the Tribune the new degree is relevant across all disciplines, from history and law to transportation and distribution. He said the system created a district-wide AI steering committee before the program, which helped articulate its position that preparing students for an AI-enabled workforce and society is essential. Potter said the college cannot shy away from the technology and must ensure students have AI competencies, including responsible and ethical use. Ayoka Noelle Mota Samuels, City Colleges' associate vice chancellor of technology sector strategy, said the system should be a place where people can afford to learn AI skills responsibly. She warned that without the education community in leadership around AI, some people could be left out.

DePaul had published a statement on AI in 2023, but Shanahan said that is like 100 years ago in this age of rapid transition. He said there has been a growing recognition over the last two years that AI does not necessarily have to be feared. While AI has brought a mix of enthusiasm, excitement, skepticism and fear, he said the advancements have benefited the institution, though he acknowledged the university is at the beginning of this. Shanahan said there will be times when it is useful to use AI and times when it is better to think your own thoughts and write your own sentences.

stories.Headline: China's trade surplus soars past $1 trillion as AI boom powers exports
stories.Summary:
China's trade surplus rose past US$1 trillion in the first 10 months of the year, customs data released on Tuesday, Nov 10, showed. A global race to build AI infrastructure lifted sales of high-tech products and helped offset weak domestic demand. Exports in October grew 35.2 per cent from a year earlier in US dollar terms, only slightly slower than the 36.3 per cent surge in September. That beat the 33.5 per cent increase economists had forecast. Exports totaled $412.3 billion in October, with growth slowing by 1.1 percentage points from September, according to Caixin Global's report.

Imports rose 41.6 per cent to $307.1 billion, speeding up from 31 per cent growth in September. The median forecast in a Reuters poll had been for a 32 per cent rise. The trade surplus for the first 10 months reached US$1.04 trillion, topping US$1 trillion for a second year in a row and hitting the milestone a month earlier than in 2025. The swelling surplus could add to tensions with the European Union, where leaders have called for more trade curbs on China. That follows an agreement with Beijing to limit Chinese exports of hybrid vehicles to the bloc over the next few years.

Because those measures have yet to take effect, factories are expected to bring forward shipments, which should support exports in the near term. China on Monday officially announced a two-month extension of its trade truce with Washington, which was due to expire on Nov 10. It said last week, though, that expanding its purchases of US farm goods would depend on the implementation of the agreed reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement. Joe Peissel, lead macroeconomist at Trivium China, said the risk of additional tariffs and other trade barriers will remain elevated in 2027, particularly as Chinese manufacturers keep expanding their presence in overseas markets.

Macquarie analysts wrote that the outlook for exports depends on how long the AI boom lasts. They expect China's exports to accelerate further in the fourth quarter before starting to slow from the first quarter of 2027. The global AI investment boom is expected to keep demand for Chinese technology products strong into 2027, but it risks deepening domestic imbalances and fuelling trade frictions with partners including the EU. The figures highlight Beijing's growing reliance on overseas demand to support an economy hobbled by subdued consumption and a protracted property slump.

Consumers remain reluctant to spend, constrained by a property downturn that has battered household wealth and dented confidence in the economic outlook. Sluggish demand at home has pushed Chinese automakers to seek sales abroad. China's car exports kept growing at a solid pace in October, according to separate industry association data, while domestic vehicle sales fell for a 12th straight month. Caixin noted, however, that car exports slowed sharply in the month.

Greater reliance on exports leaves the economy more exposed to any slowdown in global demand. The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit will take place next week in Shenzhen, a southern Chinese tech and innovation hub. Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump are expected to meet there for the third time this year. China's trade surplus hit a record US$1.2 trillion last year, according to CNA.

stories.Headline: ILION DIGITAL Cuts Ad Technical Audit Time by 94% with Launch of New AI Platform in the US
stories.Summary:
ILION DIGITAL, a performance marketing agency, announced on November 10, 2026, in New York that it has launched its proprietary digital operating system, Next Level Growth AI OS, in the US market. According to the company, the platform cuts website technical audit time by 94% and raises lead generation volume by 45%. The announcement was distributed through Newsfile Corp. Vladyslav Bilinchuk, described as the company's CEO and also as its co-founder, architected the infrastructure to reduce customer acquisition costs, limit operational errors and optimize advertising budgets. It is aimed at competitive US sectors, including e-commerce and local services.

The software integrates machine learning pipelines and artificial intelligence algorithms into an end-to-end ecosystem designed for enterprise marketing management. It is built on three synchronized internal layers: Marketing Intelligence for research and auditing, Marketing Production for programmatic asset generation, and Data Control and Learning for end-to-end telemetry oversight. The platform runs on a hybrid Human-in-the-Loop model with automated validation and direct API connections. It integrates with standard CRM systems and Google advertising APIs such as Google Ads and Google Merchant Center to automate computations and data collection. The company's in-house experts conduct the final quality audit and high-level strategic planning, which the release says significantly mitigates the risk of incorrect content.

The company reports several efficiency gains from its own deployment of the platform. The E-E-A-T Auditor, which scans landing pages across 31 technical criteria, cut a technical audit from 90 minutes to 5 minutes. The AdPilot AI campaign generation module reduced the design time for complex omnichannel advertising structures by 62%, from 25 hours to 9.5 hours, by validating 73 parameters through the API before campaigns are pushed to an account. The AI SEO Technical Specification Generator shortened the preparation of a brief from 30 minutes to 5 minutes, and at a monthly volume of 300 tasks the system frees up to 125 working hours for the team. The SearchScope AI module carries out competitive analysis and strategic website auditing in a single automated session lasting exactly 423.78 seconds.

The company also cites results for clients. In the automotive e-commerce niche, tracked conversion value rose by 39.5% over 12 months. In commercial construction services, platform integration delivered a 25% increase in generated lead volume within the first quarter after deployment. The company says the automation of routine processes aims to stabilize Return on Ad Spend and safeguard budgets against unoptimized depletion.

Bilinchuk said that packaging long-term methodologies and custom automation scripts into a single operating system let the company mitigate the linear dependency between growth in advertising volume and headcount expansion. He added that the platform acts as a technological foundation that supports a high level of analytical precision and depth in campaign execution. The company says the infrastructure is designed to align with applicable American digital services standards and enterprise-grade data privacy protocols. The release notes that its figures come from internal company data.

ILION DIGITAL describes itself as an international growth marketing agency that operates in the United States through ILION DIGITAL LLC. It offers performance marketing across paid search, paid social, SEO, Generative Engine Optimization and end-to-end web analytics. The agency has 45 in-house professionals and serves more than 60 active clients across 12 markets. It is an official Google Premier Partner 2026, which the release says places it within the top 3% of participating companies and requires a minimum 70% optimization score.
